Study LevelPhD

ApplyOfficial application page ↗

About the Position

The Nuclear Decommissioning Authority (NDA) PhD Studentship at Lancaster University focuses on understanding the longitudinal challenges of applying guardrails to Artificial Intelligence in the nuclear sector. This is a 42-month funded project, including fees and an enhanced stipend. Lancaster University invites applications for a PhD position in this area: NDA PhD Studentship: Guardrails for AI in the Nuclear Sector. Research areas covered include Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Engineering. Location: Lancaster, United Kingdom. According to the listing, funding covers the full cost of participation; financial support is listed as £21,805/year (UKRI minimum stipend 2026/27). Timing: Open - Apply as soon as possible.

Project Details

The nuclear sector is exploring the use of AI to support various functions, including operational technology (OT). Guardrails are socio-technical measures to protect systems from errant AI behaviour. This PhD will investigate a framework that supports risk-informed decisions about the choice of guardrails for ensuring safe and secure operation of nuclear functions, focusing on case studies that incorporate AI for improving security and efficiency of OT. The framework should consider characteristics of guardrails (cost, flexibility, scrutability, effectiveness) and how they are affected by longitudinal drift.

Supervisor

Professor Paul Smith, School of Computing and Communications, Lancaster University.

Entry Requirements

  • Applicants must have a Master’s degree and/or a minimum of a 2:1 in their bachelor’s degree in computer science or a related field.
  • Applicants must be resident in the UK during the period of study; they may need to travel to collect data during their studies and will need to obtain security clearance.
  • Expected primary fieldwork site will be in Cumbria.

Funding

  • 42-month funded project, including fees and an enhanced stipend.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: Open - Apply as soon as possible - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

About Lancaster University

Lancaster University is a public research university in northwest England. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across science, technology, business, humanities and social sciences. Its research includes computing, communications, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence, while its collegiate community supports interdisciplinary work and partnerships with industry, public organisations and international institutions.

Official website: https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted via the standard admissions process. You must provide an up-to-date CV, two references, a written statement of purpose, and a further piece of research/assignment work, dissertation section, or publication is recommended.
